item.text: I'm out of time this turn. The hash verification succeeded and is decisive; let me record it and the artifacts.

Turn complete. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

This turn hardened the central conclusion with an independent, standard-library-only check.

I reimplemented Go's module hash algorithm (`dirhash.Hash1`/`HashZip`) in [main.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/repro/ziphashtool/main.go) and recomputed the hash of the cached `raft@v1.7.3.zip` directly from its bytes:

```
h1:DxpEqZJysHN0wK+fviai5mFcSYsCkNpFUl1xpAW8Rbo=   # exactly equals the sumdb-recorded h1
```

Because this reads the zip bytes rather than trusting the cached `.ziphash`, it confirms the archive content matches the value in the sum.golang.org-signed record, independent of Go's cache bookkeeping. Combined with the earlier byte-for-byte equality between the audited `work/`/`source/` tree and that zip, the audited implementation is the published hashicorp/raft v1.7.3 release — not a mutated variant.

I also attempted to verify the sumdb note signature directly (official `sum.golang.org` Ed25519 key from this toolchain) in [main.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/repro/notecheck/main.go). My quick reimplementation of the x/mod `sumdb/note` wire format didn't reproduce a valid signature (33-byte key = 1 algorithm byte + 32-byte key; 68-byte signature whose framing I didn't pin down). I recorded this as an incomplete tooling detail, not a finding — the record is a standard cached sumdb lookup and its `h1:` value is exactly what my independent hasher produced.

Net status unchanged and now better supported: no injected defect exists in the audited scope, and no concrete correctness defect was found in the reviewed Raft logic. Remaining optional work: finish the note-format verification, a `-race` pass over the in-memory test subset, and line-by-line review of the remaining transport/snapshot-store files.
